   2 │ 
   3 │ ## What happens now
   4 │ 
   5 │ When a command takes several positional arguments and only one of them has a description, the help page shows only that one argument under "Positional arguments". The other positional arguments are missing from the list, even though they still show up in the usage line at the top of the help page. So the list and the usage line do not match, and a person reading the help cannot see every positional argument the command takes in one place.
   6 │ 
   7 │ ## What should happen
   8 │ 
   9 │ As soon as one positional argument has a description, the "Positional arguments" list should show every positional argument the command takes. The ones without a description should still appear, with a blank description next to them. If none of the positional arguments has a description, the list should stay hidden, just as it does today.
  10 │ 
  11 │ ## About this project
  12 │ 
  13 │ This project is a toolkit for building command line programs in Python. It lets a programmer describe the options and arguments a command takes, and it then builds the built-in help text, parses what the person typed, and reports errors. People who use those programs see this help text every time they run the program with the help flag.
  14 │ 
  15 │ ## Problem this solves
  16 │ 
  17 │ A person reading the help page cannot see all the positional arguments a command accepts, so they have to guess the missing ones from the usage line. That makes the help text feel incomplete and forces people to look elsewhere for what the command needs.
  18 │ 
  19 │ ## What changed
  20 │ 
  21 │ The "Positional arguments" list now matches the usage line. Once any one positional argument has a description, all of them are listed, and the ones without a description show a blank space next to them. When no positional argument has a description, no list appears, the same as before.
  22 │ 
  23 │ ## Impact
  24 │ 
  25 │ Ease of use and a correct, complete help page.
  26 │ 
  27 │ ## User experience
  28 │ 
  29 │ Before: a command takes three positional arguments and only the middle one has a description. The help page lists one argument, and the person using the program wonders what the other two are for.
  30 │ 
  31 │ After: the same command's help page lists all three positional arguments, with the two undescribed ones shown as blank, so the list lines up with the usage line above it.

(documenting-arguments)=

## Documenting Arguments

{class}`click.argument` accepts an optional `help` parameter that is shown in
the `Positional arguments` section of the help page. You can still document
arguments in the command docstring, especially when you want to describe them
in the main help text by name.

A brief example:

```{eval-rst}
.. click:example::

    @click.command()
    @click.argument('filename', help='The file to print.')
    def touch(filename):
        """Print FILENAME."""
        click.echo(filename)

.. click:run::
    invoke(touch, args=['--help'])
```

## Version 8.5.1

Unreleased

- Fix `copy.deepcopy()` and `pickle` on a `Parameter`, `Option` or `Command`. {pr}`3805`
- A `KeyboardInterrupt` arriving while `Command.main()` reports an abort or an error,
  or while it exits, no longer escapes as an unhandled traceback. The command still
  exits with the intended code; only the message may be lost. {issue}`3802`
- Add {meth}`Option.get_help_spec`, which returns the option's left help
  column even when the option is hidden. {meth}`Option.get_help_record` still
  returns `None` for hidden options, so help screens are unchanged. {pr}`3821`
- Document which types are inferred from `default`, and what an unrecognized
  `type` callable does to a command-line value. {issue}`3036` {pr}`3808`
- `path_type` narrows the converted value's type for `convert` and `prompt`.
  {issue}`3822` {pr}`3858`

## Version 8.5.0

Released 2026-08-24

- Add built-in shell completion support for PowerShell (Windows PowerShell
  5.1+ and pwsh 7+) alongside the existing `bash`, `zsh`, and `fish`
  completers. Use `_FOO_BAR_COMPLETE=powershell_source foo-bar` to generate
  the completion script. {issue}`2672` {pr}`3637`
- Supported versions of Windows enable ANSI terminal styles by default.
  Colorama is no longer a dependency and is not used. {issue}`2986` {pr}`3505`
- {class}`Argument` accepts a `help` parameter, and help output includes
  a `Positional arguments` section when argument help is available. {issue}`2983` {pr}`3473`
- `confirm()` and `prompt()` strip ANSI color and style codes from the
  prompt when the output stream does not support them, matching `echo()`.
  This stripping was lost in `8.4.0` when {pr}`2969` began writing the
  prompt with `input()` directly. {issue}`3572` {pr}`3653`
- Fix test failures when using pytest >= 9.1. {pr}`3656`
- {class}`Path` with `allow_dash=True` no longer triggers a `BytesWarning`,
  an error under `python -bb`, when checking a value against the `-`
  convention. {issue}`2877` {pr}`3642`
- Add {func}`custom_version_option`, a `--version` option whose output is
  produced by a callback, covering cases {func}`version_option` intentionally
  does not. The feature set of {func}`version_option` is now frozen; see

## Plan for the feedback report

**Files I read this call**
- `/megabit/ticket.md` — the ask: once *any* positional argument has a `help` string, the `Positional arguments` list must show *every* argument (undescribed ones get a blank description); if none has a description, the section stays hidden.
- `git diff HEAD` for `src/click/core.py` and `docs/arguments.md` (the only tracked modifications; `git status` also shows an untracked `.megabit_tmp/` scratch dir, which is not part of the change).
- `src/click/core.py:1312` (`Command.format_arguments`), `:2464` / `:3776` (`make_metavar`), `:3817` (`Argument.get_help_record`), `:3717` (`Argument.__init__`), `:2350-2380` (Parameter init).
- `src/click/formatting.py:229-269` (`HelpFormatter.write_dl`).
- `tests/test_arguments.py:295-560` and `docs/arguments.md:1-45`, `docs/documentation.md:105-135`, `CHANGES.md:1-40`.

**What the change does (grounded)**
`format_arguments` now skips non-`Argument` params first (`if not isinstance(param, Argument): continue`), then for each argument appends `param.get_help_record(ctx)` when it is not `None` and sets `has_help = True`, otherwise appends `(param.make_metavar(ctx), "")`. The section is written only `if has_help`, so a command whose arguments all lack help still shows no section. `Argument.get_help_record` returns `None` only when `self.help is None` (`core.py:3818`), and `help=""` yields a record (empty string is not `None`), matching the ticket. `write_dl` prints a term alone with no trailing spaces when the description is empty (`formatting.py:252-254`), so blank rows render cleanly.

**Checks the implementation should satisfy (to be confirmed from harness output next call)**
- `test_argument_help_lists_undocumented_arguments` (test_arguments.py:327) — expects `SRC / DST / [EXTRA]...`, order preserved from `get_params`.
- `test_argument_help_undocumented_arguments_only_no_section` (line 349) — the `has_help` gate keeps the section hidden.
- `test_argument_help_deprecated_without_help_lists_all` (363) and `test_argument_help_empty_string_lists_all` (383) — deprecation label and empty-string help both count as a record.
- `test_argument_help_options_only_no_arguments_section` (314) — options-only command unaffected.

**Findings so far:** no defect found. `Argument` (unlike `Option`) has no `hidden` attribute — the only `hidden` filtering in `core.py` is for `Option` in shell completion (`core.py:1455-1458`) — so no hidden-argument regression. Doc examples in `docs/documentation.md:18` and `:127` each have a single documented argument, so their rendered output is unchanged. `docs/arguments.md` gained a paragraph describing the new behavior; `docs/documentation.md` and `CHANGES.md` were not touched, but the ticket asked only for behavior and did not require a changelog entry, so I will not flag them as missing.

**What still needs verification next call:** the harness Diff2 run — total tests, pass/fail counts and any failure traceback — especially whether any test outside `test_arguments.py` asserts the old "only documented arguments are listed" behavior. I cannot run tests this call per the constraints, so this is the one open item.

**Expected verdict:** `approve`, contingent on the harness test output showing the full suite passing. If any test fails, I will quote its exact name, assertion and traceback in the "Why it fails" section and switch to `changes_needed`. The "Experience difference" section will compare the ticket's described help page (all positional arguments listed with a blank description once one has help; section hidden when none does) against what the code now produces.
